title: Spacetime From Entanglement — and 'Magic'
hook: If quantum entanglement weaves space-time together, what makes it bend into gravity? Theorists now point to a stranger ingredient they call 'magic.'
key_points: In holographic theories, entanglement between quantum bits seems to stitch space-time together.
But entanglement alone wasn't enough to explain why space-time bends — that is, gravity.
Researchers tie the bending to 'magic,' a measure of how genuinely quantum a state is.
It remains a theoretical proposal in toy models, not a tested law of our universe.
content_html: Physicists have long toyed with the idea that space-time isn't fundamental but is woven from quantum entanglement — the links that tie quantum systems together. In so-called holographic theories, knit enough entanglement among the parts and a smooth fabric of space emerges. Writing in Quanta Magazine, Charlie Wood reports that entanglement alone left a gap: it could build space-time, but it didn't explain why that fabric bends and flexes — in other words, why there's gravity.
extra_html: To close the gap, researchers point to a property with the playful name "magic": a measure of how deeply quantum a state really is, beyond the kinds of quantum behavior a regular computer could easily fake. The proposal is that this "magic" is what gives space-time its pliability, turning a rigid scaffold into something that can curve. It's worth being clear-eyed here: this is theoretical work carried out in simplified model universes, not a confirmed law of nature. The appeal is that it hints at how gravity and quantum mechanics — physics' two great frameworks — might ultimately fit together.

related.title: Quantum Entanglement
related.hook: Two particles can share one quantum state so tightly that measuring one instantly fixes the other's matching property — even light-years apart. Einstein called it spooky.

related.title: General Relativity: Gravity Is Geometry
related.hook: Einstein's biggest idea: gravity isn't a force pulling objects, it's the bending of spacetime by mass and energy. Matter curves space; curved space steers matter.
